item.title: Central North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
570
ACPN50 PHFO 250512
TWOCP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
800 PM HST Mon Aug 24 2026

For the central North Pacific...between 140W and 180W:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Lala, located several hundred miles north of Pearl and Hermes
Atoll, on Tropical Depression Moke, located several hundred miles
east of Johnston Island, on Tropical Storm Iselle, located several
hundred miles west-southwest of the southern tip of the Baja
California Peninsula, and on Tropical Depression Ten-E, located well
southwest of the southern tip of Baja California Peninsula.

Western East Pacific:
A trough of low pressure located well to the east-southeast of the
Hawaiian Islands is producing some disorganized showers and
thunderstorms. An area of low pressure is forecast to form along the
trough during the next couple of days, and environmental conditions
appear conducive for some gradual development thereafter. A tropical
depression could form during the latter part of the week or early
this weekend while the system drifts generally north-northeastward.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...20 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...50 percent.

&&
Public Advisories on Tropical Depression Ten-E are issued under
WMO header WTPZ35 NHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP5.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Depression Ten-E are issued under
WMO header WTPZ25 and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP5.

$$
Forecaster Reinhart

NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP012026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM HST Mon Aug 24 2026
 
...LALA SLIGHTLY WEAKER...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1100 PM HST...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...34.7N 175.9W
ABOUT 495 MI...800 KM N OF PEARL AND HERMES ATOLL
ABOUT 455 MI...735 KM NNE OF KURE ATOLL
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...50 MPH...85 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 325 DEGREES AT 6 MPH...9 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...994 MB...29.36 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 PM HST (0900 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Lala was 
located near latitude 34.7 North, longitude 175.9 West. Lala is 
moving toward the northwest near 6 mph (9 km/h), and this general 
motion is expected to continue for the next few days.
 
Satellite-derived wind data indicate maximum sustained winds have 
decreased to near 50 mph (85 km/h) with higher gusts. Additional 
weakening is expected during the next several days, and Lala is 
forecast to degenerate to a post-tropical remnant low by Thursday 
night.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 140 miles (220 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 994 mb (29.36 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 500 AM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Reinhart

item.title: Tropical Storm Lala Forecast Discussion Number 52
item.description:
Issued at 1100 PM HST Mon Aug 24 2026 
000
WTPA42 PHFO 250849
TCDCP2
 
Tropical Storm Lala Discussion Number  52
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP012026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM HST Mon Aug 24 2026

Lala continues to produce shallow to moderate convection in curved 
bands around its center. The coldest cloud tops are located on the 
northern side of the circulation, where recent scatterometer data 
indicate the strongest winds are occurring. There are several wind 
vectors from the ASCAT-B pass at or slightly above 40 kt, and based 
on these winds, the initial intensity is lowered to 45 kt.
 
Additional slow weakening is anticipated during the next couple of 
days while Lala moves over gradually cooler waters in a low shear 
environment. After 48 h, increasing shear along with a drier and 
more stable surrounding air mass should induce a slightly faster 
rate of weakening. These hostile conditions are expected to cause 
Lala to lose organized convection and ultimately degenerate to a 
remnant low by 72 h, if not sooner. No changes were made to the NHC 
intensity forecast or the timing of post-tropical transition.
 
Lala is moving slowly northwestward (325/5 kt) on the southwest side
of a weak mid-level ridge. This steering pattern should prevail for
the next few days, keeping Lala on a slow northwestward heading
through midweek. By days 4-5, the system is forecast to turn
northward and accelerate as the ridge builds to its east. Little
change was made to the official track forecast through 60 h, which
remains near the center of the guidance envelope. Thereafter, some
westward adjustments were made to the post-tropical portion of the
forecast to trend closer to the latest multi-model consensus aids.

MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1005 MB...29.68 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 PM HST (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Depression Moke was
located near latitude 16.0 North, longitude 163.0 West. The
depression is moving toward the west near 14 mph (22 km/h). This 
general motion is forecast to continue tonight.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 35 mph (55 km/h) with higher gusts.
Moke is expected to degenerate into a trough of low pressure 
tonight or early Tuesday.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1005 mb (29.68 inches).

item.title: Tropical Depression Moke Forecast Discussion Number 19
item.description:
Issued at 500 PM HST Mon Aug 24 2026 
164 
WTPA43 PHFO 250241
TCDCP3
 
Tropical Depression Moke Discussion Number  19
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP022026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM HST Mon Aug 24 2026

An earlier burst of convection appears to have helped Moke maintain 
its status as a tropical depression for now. ASCAT-C data near 2100 
UTC showed it still has a stretched, but well-enough defined 
circulation, with maximum believable winds near 30 kt. Therefore, 
the initial intensity is held at that value for this forecast 
advisory. Since then, another convective burst has formed north of 
Moke's center, but recent visible imagery also indicates that 
center has become less well-defined over time.

All models continue to indicate that Moke will become post-tropical 
very soon. In fact, based on recent trends it may open into a 
remnant trough of low pressure tonight before it totally loses its 
deep convection. Regardless, no significant changes were made to 
the NHC forecast with the models in good agreement on the forecast 
for the next day or so.

 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  25/0300Z 16.0N 163.0W   30 KT  35 MPH
 12H  25/1200Z 16.0N 165.0W   30 KT  35 MPH...POST-TROP/REMNT LOW
 24H  26/0000Z...DISSIPATED
